description: One bin, closed in the field, with the names of the people whose buckets are in it. THE ACCOUNTABILITY CHAIN FROM A PACK LINE BACK TO A BLOCK AND A CREW: a bin arriving at a packing house carries a tag and nothing else, and every question asked of it afterwards — whose fruit is this, which block did it come from, was that block inside a re-entry interval, who do we pay for it, and where else did that afternoon's picking go if this bin is the one that failed a residue test — is answered from this record or from nowhere. NOT A CHILD TABLE OF THE BUCKET SESSION, for the reason Shift Location Log is not a child table of the shift: a bin is sealed by a CHECKER whose phone is not editing anybody's session, several sessions tip into one bin, and one session fills many bins over a day.

fields.description: What is printed or stuck on the bin — the QR code the checker scanned, or MANUAL-XXXX where there was no tag to scan and somebody keyed one. NOT UNIQUE ON THIS SITE AND NOT MADE SO: bin tags are reused between seasons and between growers, and a uniqueness constraint would refuse the second true record rather than the first false one. `trace_bin` reports every seal carrying a tag and says how many it found, which is the honest answer to a reused tag and the one a packing house can act on.
fields.label: Bin Tag

fields.description: How many buckets were in the bin when it was closed. The figure the checker's tally showed, not a figure derived from the contributor rows — the two are allowed to disagree and the disagreement is information. A bucket tipped by somebody whose badge did not scan is in the bin and not in the rows, and a record that silently made the numbers agree would delete exactly that.
fields.label: Buckets

fields.description: Filled from the shift or the sealer on save. It is what scopes a bin to a company — a User Permission on Company reaches this doctype because this column links to one.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: When the bin was closed, which is not when the record arrived. A phone out of signal in a canyon posts an afternoon of seals the moment the bars come back, and a timestamp assigned on receipt would file the whole day at the spot where the signal returned.
fields.label: Sealed At

fields.description: The checker who closed it. A named person, because a bin count is a piece-rate figure before it is a traceability one and somebody answers for it.
fields.label: Sealed By

fields.description: Denormalised at write time, so a seal read years later names the checker as they were named then.
fields.label: Sealed By (Name)

fields.description: The shift the picking happened on. It is what joins a bin to the crew, the weather timeline and the break log for the afternoon it was filled — every exposure question about a bin is asked of a shift.
fields.label: Shift

fields.description: The block, as this app's own register names it. A Link and not a string: a residue trace runs from a bin to a block to a spray application, and a typed block name breaks that chain at its weakest point.
fields.label: Field

fields.description: The block as the CREW calls it, where that is not a Field on the register — 'the young Bings', 'row 14 east'. Kept beside the Link rather than instead of it: a record naming only a Field cannot be checked against what the checker actually said, and a record naming only a phrase cannot be joined to anything.
fields.label: Block (as called)

fields.description: The bucket session this bin's buckets were counted through, where the checker's phone was running one. Optional: a bin filled by a crew being tallied on paper is a real bin.
fields.label: Bucket Session

fields.description: What is in it, where the checker said. Free of the Field's own crop on purpose — a block is replanted and a bin sealed in 2026 holds what was picked in 2026.
fields.label: Crop

fields.description: Decimal degrees, -90 to 90. Where the bin was standing when it was closed, which is a stronger claim than which block it was picked from: a bin is sealed at the end of a row and a coordinate is what puts it there.
fields.label: Latitude

fields.description: Decimal degrees, -180 to 180. Negative in the western hemisphere: a Pacific Northwest orchard reads about -121, and a positive number there is a coordinate in China.
fields.label: Longitude

fields.description: The horizontal accuracy the phone reported, in metres. Kept and never used as a gate — the same argument Shift Location Log makes: a fix under a canopy reads badly and is still the only record of where the bin was.
fields.label: Accuracy (metres)

fields.description: Computed at resolution 10 where the coordinates allow it, so a bin can be joined against a Field's or a Parcel's stored coverage without loading a polygon — which is how a bin whose `field` was left blank is still placed on the ground. Blank on a site without the h3 package: the coordinates are the record and this is the index.
fields.label: H3 Cell (res 10)

fields.description: The workers whose badges were scanned into this bin since the last seal. THIS TABLE IS THE FEATURE: everything else here can be reconstructed from a shift and a tag, and this cannot be reconstructed from anything once the crew has gone home.
fields.label: Contributors

fields.description: Where the seal came from. iOS is the ordinary case — a checker closing a bin on the tally screen. Manual is somebody entering it afterwards, and it is a different kind of evidence: worth keeping, worth being able to tell apart.
fields.label: Source

fields.description: The identifier the handset generated for this seal before it sent it. IT IS WHAT MAKES A RETRY SAFE: a phone that sealed a bin and did not hear the answer sends the same call again, and without this the orchard gets two records of one bin and the packing house gets a doubled count. Unique where present.
fields.label: Client Event ID

fields.description: The id of the kind-4004 NOSTR event the handset published for this seal, where it published one. Recorded and never required: the relay is a distribution channel and this record is the register, and a bin sealed while the relay was unreachable is still a sealed bin.
fields.label: NOSTR Event ID
Notes
fields.description: Anything the checker wants on the record — a bin topped up from another row, a tag that would not scan, a bucket somebody could not account for.

name: Bin Seal
